articles.title: TERRAFORM INTRODUCES TFPOLICY SUPPORT FOR STACKS, SCIM SUPPORT, AND MORE
articles.summary: HashiCorp made HCL-based policy for Terraform Stacks generally available, along with multi-deployment group orchestration and agent-ready CLI commands with JSON output. SCIM 2.0 provisioning also reached general availability for HCP Terraform Standard and Premium.

articles.title: THE BEST OCTOPUS YET
articles.summary: Octopus Deploy redesigned its interface with instance-wide search, regrouped navigation, and a searchable REST API reference covering about 1,800 endpoints. The update is rolling out to Octopus Cloud now and will reach self-hosted customers in Octopus Server 2027.0 on December 2.

articles.title: DEDICATED CLUSTERS PER WORKLOAD: WHEN SHARED STOPS PAYING
articles.summary: Shared Kubernetes clusters are the right default, but some workloads need dedicated ones. Blast radius, network reach, and regulatory boundaries justify separation, though duplicated components and upgrades add cost teams often underestimate.

articles.title: DOGFOODING CHECKS AND WORKSPACES: HARD LESSONS FROM 3,000 REPOS
articles.summary: Chainguard moved thousands of daily builds off GitHub Actions onto its own microVM infrastructure to prevent release queues from stalling during cloud outages. CVE-remediation agents now run at 97 to 98 percent weekly success rates, with package bumps auto-merging about 99 percent of the time.

articles.title: PLAID BUILT $382K IN PIPELINE FROM ONE TLDR PLACEMENT
articles.summary: Close Q4 with proof. TLDR reaches 8 million tech readers across 14 newsletters. Book a Q4 campaign [8].

articles.title: STITCH-SKILLS
articles.summary: stitch-skills is a library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, and Cursor.

articles.title: DOCKER COMPOSE LINTER
articles.summary: Docker Compose Linter checks Compose files for configuration errors, style violations, and common pitfalls. It supports configurable rules, automatic fixes for selected issues, and integration with local development, pre-commit hooks, and CI pipelines. Automated sorting preserves comments.

articles.title: BECOME A FOUNDING MEMBER OF TLDR'S COMMUNITY (2 MINUTE FORM)
articles.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss best practices and the latest AI news. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR. Apply here to join [12].

articles.title: WHY YOUR CI PIPELINE FAILED: DECODING EXIT STATUS 1 & OOM
articles.summary: Harness shows how identical exit status 1 failures in parallel CI stages hid different root causes. A full disk, an out-of-memory kill, and a timed-out database wait each needed different fixes, so teams should read stage logs rather than banners.

articles.title: PLEASE DON'T GIVE THE ROBOT MY SSH KEYS: HOW TO KEEP AI OUT OF TROUBLE
articles.summary: Teleport field CTO Boris Kurktchiev explains delegated identity for AI agents. Agents start without access, request only what a task needs, and leave an audit trail linking their actions to the person who assigned the work.

articles.title: HOW THE DATA CENTER SHAPES THE AI WORKLOAD
articles.summary: Network topology shapes how multi-node GPU workloads distribute computation and move data. Larger NVLink domains change where communication-heavy parallelism can run, while SHARP performs collective aggregation inside switches. Nscale's engineering overview connects these architectural choices to practical questions about GPU placement, fabric configuration, and cluster validation.

articles.title: IS YOUR CODE PROTECTED FROM DAY ONE?
articles.summary: Security as an afterthought means patches at midnight. Microsoft Azure helps make protection part of your dev lifecycle with Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Ship fast. Ship safely. Get started with Azure →

articles.title: CAN EUROPEAN IT LEADERS PROVE AI ROI TO THE BOARD?
articles.summary: A CloudBees survey of 450 European IT leaders shows 69% expect boards to demand AI ROI proof by 2027, yet only 43% could show it within a month.

articles.title: WHY ONLY 19% OF BACKEND DEVELOPERS SAY THEY USE KUBERNETES
articles.summary: A State of Cloud Native Development report found that 93% of organizations use DevOps standardization, yet only 19% of backend developers say they use Kubernetes.

articles.title: OUTGROWING LAMBDA FUNCTIONS, NOT LAMBDA
articles.summary: Honeycomb moved its query processing from AWS Lambda Functions to Lambda Managed Instances to address scaling limits and rising costs.
